On 2026-11-02 evening, after seeing canvas version 73, Kenneth corrected the credits design in four ways:

- Every credit is the same. No Standard-only ("basic_only", "trickle") lot. Free accounts (not subscribed) get 50 credits a month, expiring one month after grant, that pay for either tier. Not "everyone": he told the design session "the 'everyone gets 50 credits' wording is wrong. I never said that." I had told the design session "yes, everyone" as my own pick before he answered; never pass my pick on as his. His words: "let's just give free users 50/mo use-it-or-loose it credits".
- Workshop has no ceiling. "no ceiling. It's probably easier just to say standard messages cost 0 credits". Nothing about 600 or fair use remains.
- A balance is one number of credits, never "N Standard or N Expert messages" beside it ("showing a number of messages and credits at the same time is fucking confusing"). The translation line was my addition in the design doc, never his decision. Bars are grouped only by expiry; bought credits get a bar too (decision 13 closed).
- "New Standard chat" and board 3d are gone, since the case only existed because of the Standard-only lot.

Prices in messages appear only where the person chooses or is stopped: picker options, the stop card for the chat's tier, the pricing page's one sentence, the low-balance notice, and one scale line under the first-month offer.

**Why:** he said he was "seriously worried that we are not on the same page" and asked me to restate the plan; the Standard-only lot and the ceiling were placeholders the plan carried without his words behind them.

**How to apply:** before presenting any credits surface, check it against these four. When a plan carries a mechanism (a lot kind, a cap) with no quote from Kenneth behind it, flag it as mine rather than drawing it on every board. Related: [[credit-price-needs-its-unit]], [[usage-against-quota-common-shape]], [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].

Later the same evening Kenneth reviewed every mechanism that was mine, not his. Kept: the launch offer, "About 25 credits left" (credits, not messages), "Expiring credits are used first", the savings switch on by default, the Account page shape, Standard as the default tier after the first month, the v1 welcome-back fill-ins, the print-report form details, the alias ids. Expiry: every expiring lot expires one month from the day it was granted, never at a calendar month end. His message was only a keep list, so anything left off it counts as dropped. A session wrongly called the report rules "neither kept nor dropped"; he corrected that the same day: "I thought the clawback are removed, rigth? And why is it still a placeholder?" The clawback is removed. Asked about 25 credits, three a day and stopping after two invalid reports, he ruled: "Remove these. only keep the 1st one". A report earns 25 credits, one per G-code, and a review is only recorded.

Ruled later: "no 50 credits for first month. only 500 initial credits. pack holders also get 50 credits a month." The 50 a month goes to every account not on a subscription, starting after the first month; the balance example is 62 + 500 = 562 with no Free credits bar.

      same OAuth token as the browser sign-in. Wrong code, a spent code, too many
      codes, wrong password and too many tries stay on their step; anything else
      ends with one generic error.
    - Google opens /accounts/google/login/ with next= the authorize address, so
      the browser goes straight to Google and back. PKCE, state and the loopback
      callback are unchanged.
    - JusPrin is a syndicate of its own on the server, which picks it by host: the
      gateway and the sign-in server move from app.obico.io to jusprinv2.obico.io.
      v1's Obico account is no longer a JusPrin account, so the v1 import no
      longer carries v1's token or server, and v1 users sign up again.
    - Until jusprinv2.obico.io is live in production, a build signs in only with
      JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT pointing at staging (jusprinv2-stg.obico.io).

    characters, fake-printer control writes within one second ignored), and
    --fresh-example signs in by email against a stand-in gateway. A dialog log
    line in DialogListeners.cpp no longer names OrcaSlicer, which AgentUI's
    wording guard flagged.
    
    Tested on macOS: agent_bridge_tests (554 cases, with the coordinator fix that
JusPrin Cloud account: credits, the first launch, and sign-in by email and Google at jusprinv2.obico.io

Credits. The app shows and spends JusPrin Cloud credits; every credit is the
same, and a balance is one number of credits.
- Model pickers show each model's price, and are greyed once the chat has a
  message. The balance shows as a ring with a hover panel: one bar per lot,
  grouped by expiry, bought credits included. A message that can't be paid
  for offers "Get more credits"; a 402 from the gateway ends in a failed card.
  "About 25 credits left" shows once at 25 credits or less.
- A new account chat starts on Expert while a first-month lot is live, and on
  Standard after it. A Standard chat leaves out the picture tools; a picture
  there shows as a warning on its chip, with Remove.
- Turns the app starts itself send X-JusPrin-Request: note and run on Expert
  without changing the chat's model. RecordConversion turns one provider
  format's stored turn into the other's, byte for byte, so caches still hit.
- A turn that polls for its own slice is answered with busy, and the third
  refused poll ends the turn.
- Print history has a report form with a photo; every report earns 25 credits.
The gateway side (ledger, Chargebee, the pricing page) is on tsd-enterprise
branch claude/credits-ledger. The welcome-back window's kept-price box stays
hidden behind V1_PRICE_CARRIES_OVER until then.

First launch: Welcome, then Printers, then Home, as on the canvas's "On
boarding experience" page.
- Welcome: the lockup, a placeholder clip with its photo credits, "The AI
  slicer that fixes failed prints." and four doors: sign in, your own API key,
  Claude Code or Claude Desktop, and Just slice.
- Printers: "Bring your printers from OrcaSlicer?" when an OrcaSlicer folder
  sits beside the data folder; otherwise the Agent page's add-printer form,
  with "Skip, use a default", which installs Generic Klipper and marks that
  printer "assumed" on its Home card. Skipped when a JusPrin v1 import or an
  opened file already brought a printer. After an import, a result screen
  lists each printer and process preset as imported, imported as
  "<name> (Orca copy)", or not imported with the reason. OrcaSlicer's
  PresetBundle::import_presets is unchanged: OrcaImport.cpp gives a taken name
  a renamed copy first, so it has nothing to ask.
- Home: an Agent group above Printers shows "Set up the agent" with the three
  doors, or the account and its credit bars after signing in.
- OnboardingModel decides the step from saved progress; onboarding is saved as
  completed only once Home is reached, and the earlier "dismissed" status
  counts as completed. ShellController::open_preferences can open Preferences
  for one task and report "key", "tool" or nothing.
- The add-printer form is AgentUI's AddPrinterForm in a shadow root, and its
  host is the printer chat's conversation with no thread and no model: it has
  no messages and no tool call to finish.
- resources/jusprin/welcome/welcome-clip.mp4 is a PLACEHOLDER animatic, to be
  replaced by a recording of the real app; its two #3DBenchy photos are
  CC BY 2.0, credited in that folder's README and on the welcome.

Sign-in. The door on the welcome and on Home offers "Continue with Google" and
"Continue with email".
- Email signs in through django-allauth's API for apps under
  ent/jusprin/v2/auth/: "Email me a 6-digit code" (which also makes the
  account for a new address) or a password with Forgot password. It brings the
  same OAuth token as the browser sign-in. Wrong code, a spent code, too many
  codes, wrong password and too many tries stay on their step; anything else
  ends with one generic error.
- Google opens /accounts/google/login/ with next= the authorize address, so
  the browser goes straight to Google and back. PKCE, state and the loopback
  callback are unchanged.
- JusPrin is a syndicate of its own on the server, which picks it by host: the
  gateway and the sign-in server move from app.obico.io to jusprinv2.obico.io.

  longer carries v1's token or server, and v1 users sign up again.

  JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT pointing at staging (jusprinv2-stg.obico.io).

characters, fake-printer control writes within one second ignored), and

"""What GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account answers: numbers and names only, so the app
can keep reading it for years."""
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Count, Sum
from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone

from app_ent.models import Subscription
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .ledger import active_v2_plan, ensure_lots, live_lots
from .models import CreditCharge, CreditGrant
from .reports import report_activity

USAGE_DAYS = 30


def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    return {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }


def _plan(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    subscription = Subscription.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    return {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': bool(subscription and subscription.active()),
        'auto_reload': False,
    }


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def _usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    # The gateway never sees a chat's title, so a row names the chat by its id.
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'tier': row['tier'],
                 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity += report_activity(user, now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or lot.expires_at is not None]
    return {
        'credits': {'total': sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots), 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': _plan(user),
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': _usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
    }

- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the

- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;

of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166

and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear

result.output:
## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. - `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
metadata:

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Five traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
---
name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6b96dccc-1cb4-4f72-9de4-3ecee4b28e74
  modified: 2026-09-08T05:58:16.222Z
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

        self.wfile.write(body)
    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()

content.text:
"See usage" now opens an Account page that shows your credits and what you spent them on. Before, it showed nothing because of two gaps. The Preferences window never asked the server for your account. And nothing drew the 30 days of usage the server already sends with every account answer.

**What Account shows now** (matches the Account boards on the design canvas)
- Your plan: "Pay as you go", or the plan's name and when it renews. A "Get more credits" button opens the pricing page.
- Credits left, with one bar per kind of credit, the same bars the message box's credit popup uses.
- Usage: credits spent in the last 30 days, a bar per day (hover a bar to see that day's total), and a table of date, chat, tier, messages and credits. The table shows 5 rows, and "See all activity" shows the rest. Print reports appear as "+25" rows.

**How chats get their names.** The server records which chat spent credits only as a hashed id and never sees the chat's title. So the app now keeps a small file of chat titles under the same id (`jusprin/chat-titles.json` in the data folder). It updates the file whenever a chat's list or title changes, and sends the matching titles along with the account. A chat the app has no title for reads "A chat not on this computer". That will happen for your 10 credits until you open the project that holds those chats once, because the file is new.

**Tested**
- Page tests: 673 on the Agent page, including three new ones for Account, and 154 on the Home page. One new test sets the time zone to US Pacific and checks the dates. Without reading dates as UTC, it fails.
- Host tests: 555, including a new one that checks the titles file and the titles sent with the account. The design-token and theme tests also pass.
- In the built app, on a scratch copy, I pointed the app at a small local server answering with sample usage. The screenshot I sent shows the result. The Preferences window asked for the account on its own, and its own empty chat was not added to the titles file.
- I haven't tried it against staging with your real account. I couldn't scroll inside the window from here, so the print-report row and the untitled-chat row were checked only by the page tests.

**Left out, because nothing in the app supports them yet:**
- For a plan holder, the price and a "Manage plan" button.
- "Bought 500 credits" rows. The server doesn't send purchases in its usage list.
- The "Alert me when a subscription would save me money" checkbox. No such setting exists in the app.

**Other things I chose:**
- The gap between chart bars is 4px rather than the board's 2px. The stylesheet guard only allows spacing from 4px up.
- Each time Preferences opens, it now also asks the server for its model lists. That's a side effect of how I gave the window its account fetch.
- I added one design token, the chart height of 88px, with its guard.
Show the screenshots so that I can review them.

## 5. Account endpoint and balance display

### 5.1 `GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account`

New Django view (plain request handling, on `tsdweb-prod`, next to `/models`), bearer-authenticated like `/models`:

```json
{
  "credits": {"total": 562, "lots": [  // no free lot in the first month
      {"kind": "signup", "credits": 62, "granted": 500, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"},
      {"kind": "pack", "credits": 500, "granted": 500, "expires_at": null}]},
  "plan": {"id": "jusprin-workshop-monthly", "name": "Workshop", "renews_at": "...", "unlimited_basic": true,
           "obico_discount": true,
           "auto_reload": false},
  "prices": {"credit_cents": 2, "pack": {"credits": 500, "cents": 1000},
             "plans": [{"id": "jusprin-hobby-monthly", "name": "Hobby", "cents": 1000, "credits": 750},
                       {"id": "jusprin-workshop-monthly", "name": "Workshop", "cents": 2000, "credits": 1000, "unlimited_basic": true}]},
  "usage_30d": {"basic_turns": 140, "expert_turns": 60, "credits": 440,
                "days": [{"date": "2026-11-19", "credits": 60}, ...],
                "activity": [{"date": "2026-11-19", "chat": "Resizing a Print to Fit the Bambu A1 mini", "tier": "expert", "messages": 12, "credits": 60}]},
  "suggestion": {"plan": "jusprin-hobby-monthly", "saves_cents_per_month": 380}
}
```

`days` and `activity` feed the Account page's usage chart and table (boards 4b, 4c: a total for 30 days, a bar per day, a row per chat with tier, messages and credits, plus reward rows). The composer's hover panel needs only `credits` and `plan`.

`/jusprin/api/me/` stays as the sign-in check; the app calls `/account` after a sign-in check, after every completed or failed turn on the `jusprin` provider (one small GET, no streaming change), when the Preferences account section opens, and when the window regains focus after the person was sent to the browser to buy. A cheaper later step is a `X-JusPrin-Credits` response header on the stream start, but `AgentTransport` does not surface response headers today, so the GET comes first.

### 5.2 In the app

Synced to canvas version 79 (Kenneth's review, 2026-11-02). The boards are the source of truth for wording; `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md` lists them per point.

- **A chat keeps its model** (Kenneth, 2026-11-02, "for now"): the tier is chosen before the person's first message in a chat and never changes after. A turn the app started (the file-opened report) does not count: it runs on Expert and leaves the pickers live (3.3). Once a chat has a message from the person, the model and thinking pickers stay in the composer, greyed, and hovering shows a two-line tooltip: "A chat keeps the model and thinking level it started with. Start a new chat to change them." / "Each message you send in this chat costs 5 credits." (board 2c). `Composer.tsx` today disables the pickers only while the Agent responds; that becomes "disabled once the chat has a message". `chat-history-cache-plan.md` D5 (a switch within one wire format) is superseded for now.
- **Model picker** (`ModelPickers.tsx`): each option shows its price from `ModelOptionInfo.credits` with its unit, "Expert · 5 credits a message" and "Standard · 1 credit a message" (never "1 credit" alone), plus one clause on when to use it. On Workshop the Standard option reads "Standard · 0 credits a message". Only Expert has a thinking picker. BYOK options show no price. The option stays this short; Kenneth rejected a clause about pictures (2026-11-02).
- **A picture in a Standard chat** (decided 2026-11-02, board 3e): the staged attachment row (`AttachmentChip.tsx`: thumbnail, name, second line, Remove) carries the notice. In a chat whose model has `images: false`, a staged picture keeps its thumbnail, its second line reads "Standard can't see pictures, so this one will not be sent.", styled as the design system's warning (triangle-alert glyph in status-warning beside primary ink), and Remove is the only action on the row (Kenneth: "remove 'new expert chat' button"). Send stays enabled; the gateway drops the image blocks and leaves its text note (3.4). The host also leaves the picture-returning tools (`view_render` and the others that return images) out of a Standard chat's tool list, keyed on the model's `images` flag from `GET /models`.

Hover or tap opens the panel: "562 credits left." The boards exist (canvas version 79, captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/`); the tooltip on 2c needs two lines where the design system's tooltip has one, so that is a token change first.

### 5.3 The "subscription would save you money" alert (decided)

Computed server-side in `/account` from the last 30 days of `CreditCharge`:

- cost at the Pay as you go price = credits × 2¢;
- cost on Hobby = $10 + max(0, credits − 750) × 2¢;
- cost on Workshop = $20 + max(0, expert credits − 1,000) × 2¢ (basic turns cost 0);
- apply the 20% Obico discount when it applies;
- `suggestion` names the cheapest plan when it saves at least $3 a month against what the person is doing now (pack, or current plan). It never names Pay as you go: the reverse alert, telling a subscriber that Pay as you go would cost less, was removed with board 7c.

The app shows it once as a dismissable line above the composer and in Preferences › Account, re-evaluated when the 30-day window changes the answer. Preferences › Account has the switch "Alert me when a subscription would save me money", on by default (the message is in the person's favour; the switch exists so it can be silenced). The caveat from the brainstorm stands: this recruits exactly the heavy users, which is why the plans give 1.5× and not 2× the pack rate.

### 5.4 Where the Account and pricing pages render (recommend: the server)

**Not decided. Do not build either way until Kenneth chooses (decision 12 in section 12).** What follows is a recommendation with its reasons, not the plan.

Kenneth asked (2026-11-02) whether the server should serve the account and pricing pages into a webview instead of the app building them from the `/account` API. His reasons: pricing will be experimented with a lot, so changing it must not need an app release, and old app versions must not keep showing stale prices. I agree, and recommend this split:

- **Composer: API.** The ring, the hover panel, the picker prices and the pre-send check render inside the composer on every keystroke and must degrade when offline, so they stay on `/account` and `/models`. That API returns numbers and names only, which keeps it cheap to hold backward compatible.
- **Account and pricing: server pages in a webview.** Boards 4a to 4c and 5a, 5b become one web page under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` (templates or the existing Vue app, rendered with the person's data), opened in a second `AgentWebView` from Preferences › Account and from every "Get more credits". The desktop implementation of those boards moves from the client repo to tsd-enterprise. Steam does exactly this for its store and account pages inside the native client.
- **Signing the webview in:** the app holds an OAuth bearer token; the page needs a session. Never put the token in the URL (it ends up in logs). New endpoint `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/webview_session` (bearer): returns a single-use URL valid for 60 seconds; the webview opens it, the view logs the session in with Django's `login()` and redirects to the page. This endpoint is the real new cost, about a day with tests (single use, expiry, wrong user).
- **Theme and tokens:** the app passes `?theme=light|dark` and the page uses the same token CSS as the Agent page (`bundle.css` variables), so it is not a second design system.
- **Checkout stays in the system browser:** the served pricing page hands off to Chargebee's hosted page in the default browser, as section 4 already says; my expectation, not verified, is that 3-D Secure redirects are what breaks inside embedded webviews. The app refreshes `/account` on window focus.
- **Bridge contract:** two messages from the page to the app, `credits_changed` and `close`, and nothing else, so a three-year-old app still works with today's page. The page never calls back into the host for data.
- **Offline:** the page shows a plain "can't reach JusPrin" state with a retry, not a browser error; the composer keeps the last `/account` answer.
- **Latency:** a remote page takes a visible moment to appear in Preferences › Account; acceptable there, which is one more reason the composer stays on the API.

Your own API key · one row per provider

Decided 2026-10-21; replaces the provider tabs. Every provider has its own row, so you can see at a glance which ones have a key. Agent setup and Preferences › Agent use the same row (Design System › Agent/Provider Row). The app keeps each provider’s key on this computer and can show its start and last 4 characters; it records no dates, so none are shown. Key characters are examples.
1. No key
Only Add key. Nothing looks filled in.
2. Entering a key
Placeholder text only, no bullets: an empty field never looks filled in. Paste sits in the field; Check key waits for a key.
3. Checking
The key being checked stays visible and locked, so it is clear which one is in question. Cancel stops the check.
4. Couldn’t check
The provider couldn’t be reached. Nothing was saved, so this isn’t a rejection.
5. Key saved
A saved key is read-only: its start and last 4 characters at full contrast. It never shows as bullets.
6. Replacing
Replace opens an empty field for the new key. The saved key stays until the new one passes its check; Cancel keeps it.
7. Rejected
The provider refused the saved key. Its last 4 characters stay visible so the person knows which key failed.
8. Working until restart
The key passed but couldn’t be stored on this computer. It works now and will be asked for again after a restart.

commit 641c17f13e46a2deefccf1d886eec9e7091f0ed5
Author: Kenneth Jiang <k@obico.io>
Date:   Fri Oct 23 02:05:19 2026 +0000

    Add JusPrin's own Preferences window
    
    JusPrin's Preferences replaces OrcaSlicer's dialog for everyday use. It is
    one window that opens over any screen, from the gear on Home and from
    Preferences... in a project's menu. It is a
    React page (PreferencesApp) driven by PreferencesWindow, with every setting
    read and written through PreferencesSettings on the same AppConfig keys
    OrcaSlicer uses, so the classic view and JusPrin agree.
    
    Sections: Account, Agent (the shared Agent connection rows), Appearance,
    3D view, Projects & files and Updates. Nothing about Bambu Cloud and no
    expert options; "OrcaSlicer preferences..." opens OrcaSlicer's dialog
    unchanged. Dark mode calls the same OrcaSlicer functions the dialog's
    checkbox does. The language list is built from the installed
    translations; a new language is saved at once and takes effect when
    JusPrin restarts ("Restart now" or "Later"), because rebuilding the window
    in place left the old Edge process on the old language and every web page
    then failed to load. Restart now saves the project and starts a fresh
    JusPrin with the same command line; if the save is refused, JusPrin stays
    open and says why. The design is the "Preferences" page on the JusPrin v2
    canvas (2026-10-21).

input.recap: The Preferences design comparison is done. Six features on the boards are missing from the app: four were held back with the unbuilt billing work, and two Preferences rows have no recorded reason. Nothing new was changed, and the usage work is still not committed.
input.ask: Should I add the missing account-details and default-thinking rows to Preferences?

content.text:
Usage was missing on purpose. The credits plan put "the served Account and pricing pages" in a later step, together with Chargebee billing. That step was waiting on an open decision: should the Account and pricing pages be web pages served by our server into the app, or be built inside the app? The credits session built everything else, pointed "See usage" at an Account page that had no usage yet, and listed step 3 as "not here" in its commit message. I couldn't find any later answer from you on that decision, in memory or in code.

So I looked for everything else that was held back with step 3, and then compared every Preferences board with the code.

**Missing because they were held back with billing:**

1. **The plan price and a "Manage plan" button** (board 4c, "Workshop · $16 a month"). Billing doesn't exist yet, so there is no plan to manage.
2. **The savings alert.** On boards 7a and 7b, a pay-as-you-go user sees one line above the message box, such as "Hobby would have saved you $5.00 in the last 30 days", with "See the sums" and "Subscribe". Preferences › Account would have the switch "Alert me when a subscription would save me money", on by default. You kept this on 11-02. Neither side is built: the server's account endpoint always returns `suggestion: None`.
3. **The "+500 credits" line** that board 9 shows when you come back from buying. There's no buying yet. Related, and from my own work: the Agent page fetches the account again when its window gets focus, but the Preferences window doesn't. Once buying exists, Account would show the old balance until you reopen it.
4. **"Bought N credits" rows** in the usage table. The server doesn't send them.

**Missing from Preferences, reason unknown:**

5. **Account section:** an "Email and account details" row ("Change your email or delete your account in your browser", with an "Open in browser" button), and the line "Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this computer." Neither has ever been in the code.
6. **Agent › "New chats start with":** the board has a Thinking row ("Higher levels answer more carefully, and more slowly", default Medium). The code only has Model.

The Preferences window was built on 10-23. My earliest saved copy of that board is from 11-01, so I can't tell whether these rows were added to the board later or skipped when it was built.

**Differences that are deliberate, so not missing:**
- **Language:** the board says the window reloads. The code asks you to restart instead. Commit 641c17f13e4 explains why: reloading in place left the embedded browser on the old language, and every web page then failed to load.
- **The Model row's hint:** the code says "A chat keeps the model it started with." That follows your 11-02 rule. The board's "Any chat can switch from its message box" is out of date.
- **The "This model needs an OpenAI key… Add a key…" notice** on the board about where Preferences opens isn't in the code. I haven't checked whether the model picker can still reach that state, so it may be obsolete.

The other sections match their boards: Appearance (apart from Language), 3D view, Projects & files, Updates in all five states, the sign-in states and the API key rows.

**Decision needed: should the Account and pricing pages stay in the app, or move to web pages our server shows inside the app?** This is your call because it decides which repository the billing screens get built in. input.recap: I couldn't find any session where the default Thinking row in Preferences was discussed or removed. No commit ever had the row, and the live design board still shows it. Nothing was changed.
input.ask: Should the Preferences board drop its Thinking row so it matches the app?

content.text:
I couldn't confirm it. No session I can search shows you, or an agent, deciding to drop the default Thinking row from Preferences. The evidence points the other way: the row has never been in the code, and the design board still has it.

**Where I looked:**
- **What you typed in every JusPrin session**, including the worktree sessions. I searched for "thinking" next to words like Preferences, default, new chat or remove, and also for "effort" and "reasoning". The only hits were unrelated: one about the model's output limit on 10-20, and one about hiding the "Thinking:" label when the pane is narrow.
- **The row's own text**, "Higher levels answer more carefully, and more slowly". It only shows up in sessions that dumped the board's text. Nobody discussed it.
- **Git history on every branch.** No commit has ever contained a Thinking row for Preferences. The window was built on 10-23 with only the Model row, and its commit message doesn't mention leaving Thinking out.
- **The design board itself.** The live Preferences board still draws the row under "New chats start with", default Medium. If it had been removed in design, the board would most likely have lost it.
- **All 16 comment threads on the design canvas.** None is about Preferences or a default thinking level.

**What does exist, and might be what you're remembering:**
- **The 11-02 comment on board 7a.** You asked to keep the model and thinking pickers in the message box, greyed out once a chat has started, with a tooltip. That's about the pickers in each chat, not the Preferences default.
- **The 11-02 pricing decision:** "Thinking picker on Standard: Expert only." Standard has no thinking levels, so a single default level for new chats only fits Expert and API-key models. My guess is that this makes the row awkward, but I found nothing saying it was removed for that reason.

The 10-21 to 10-23 session that built the window may have talked about it, but I couldn't find that session's transcript. The 10-23 session I did find read the board right before the commit, but it was working on agent setup and never mentions the row.
Yes, drop it

**Fixed:** the Preferences window didn't fetch the account again when it got the focus back. Say you have Preferences › Account open, click "Get more credits", buy in the browser and come back. Account would still show the old balance until you closed and reopened Preferences. The chat panel already fetches the balance again when it gets the focus; Preferences now does the same.

I wrote a test first, saw it fail, then added the fix to `PreferencesApp.tsx`. All 674 page tests pass and the type check is clean. I haven't rebuilt the app to try it there. The app-side code that answers the request is the same code the chat panel already uses.

   - an "Email and account details" row with an "Open in browser" button, for changing your email or deleting your account;
   - the line "Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this computer."
5. **The open decision on whether the server or the app draws the Account and pricing pages.** Four Account features wait on it: the plan price with "Manage plan", the savings alert and its switch, the "+500 credits" line after buying, and "Bought N credits" rows.

2026-11-03 Kenneth's words: "full syndicate with its own accounts." He was choosing between this and a proposal to keep JusPrin accounts in the base Obico pool with JusPrin as a branding-only syndicate (report: side-session-notes/local_cea7b182-1404-4ee3-afa3-e87cbafe7c2d/jusprin-syndicate-one-account-report.md). The report had recommended branding-only; he overruled it.

**Why:** syndicates were designed for branding plus per-brand trickle emails; a separate pool means Obico's trial and drips (which filter on syndicate base) skip JusPrin accounts with no special-casing. This replaces the reverted per-path trial skip (tsd-enterprise 5daee67e1b, reverted by cf01e7adbf).

**How to apply:** an Obico user signing in to JusPrin gets a separate JusPrin account; that is accepted, not a bug. Existing JusPrin v1 users (base-syndicate accounts today; v1 branding comes from a User-Agent check in app/context_processors.py, no syndicate DB row exists): 2026-11-04 Kenneth: "We will tell JusPrin v1 users to re-sign up. We will also manually migrate their subscriptions. The V1 data won't be migrated." So no data-migration code is needed. Related: [[allauth-65-upgrade]].

**2026-11-04 Kenneth picked the host: "jusprin.obico.io"** (staging jusprin-stg.obico.io, my proposal, not his words). Why a host and not the X-Obico-Syndicate header: the app's browser sign-in runs in the system browser, which can't send headers, and an app.obico.io session would authorize /o/authorize/ as the Obico account. Apple sign-in: JusPrin's own sign-in page simply has none (Kenneth). Implemented, committed, not pushed or applied: tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-syndicate` (set_up_jusprin_syndicate command, jusprin_subscription_status lists both accounts), JusPrin `claude/elated-sutherland-84a741` 48c7b684f5 (default gateway jusprin.obico.io; v1 import no longer carries v1's token or jusprin_server), ops `claude/jusprin-host` acc4494 (ingress, managed cert, RUNBOOK rollout steps). Local DB has the jusprin syndicate on jusprin.localhost:3334. Test-DB trap: syndicate id sequence starts at 1 beside base's explicit id 1.

**2026-11-04 later, Kenneth renamed the hosts: "use jusprinv2.obico and jusprinv2-stg.obico so that they are separate from v1."** Staging site, ingress, cert (gke-managed-cert-jusprinv2-app-stg), Google redirect moved; DNS jusprinv2-stg pending Namecheap sign-in. He also had me revert (delete, never pushed) an obico-server change that hid the login page's "use your Obico account" sentence; the sentence is keyed to the jusprin syndicate, not the host, so it still shows on jusprinv2-stg. Commits unpushed: ops c0f2b61, JusPrin a5b10e2f01, tsd-enterprise 6a3d8172aa. Test trap: a new Site joins the first syndicate (base) on save.

**2026-11-04, Kenneth: "JusPrin v1 and v2 are completely different branding; we shouldn't share the same branding whatsoever ... create a new syndicate for JusPrin v2 and everything should derive from there."** The `jusprin` name/brand (SYNDICATES['jusprin'], old star logo, obico-server templates' jusprin blocks, the v1 User-Agent hack) is v1's. v2 = syndicate `jusprinv2`, SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'] in web_ent/settings_ent.py, soft-serve lockup at web_ent/jusprin/static/jusprinv2/img/, command set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate. Pushed to tsd-enterprise master; staging DB syndicate renamed jusprinv2 (id 3).

**2026-11-05, Kenneth: "Yes, add it" (JusPrin 2's own look in obico-server).** obico-server f78ef6e8 on master: jusprinv2 in color-scheme.js singleThemeSyndicates (light only), colors in static/js/syndicate.js from JusPrin's design-tokens.json, syndicateText.js entry, non_vue_layout.html hides Obico's navbar. Release without touching the shared checkout (its obico-server sits on another branch, so release.sh refuses): tsd-enterprise worktree at origin/master with obico-server replaced by a symlink to an obico-server worktree, npm ci both + npm run build, then rm the symlink (git refuses a symlinked submodule path), write builds/last_*_commit.txt, commit "Check in built bundles", push -f origin HEAD:release. Missing favicon.png for a syndicate = 500 from ManifestStaticFilesStorage; tests don't catch it without a finders test. **Model hint:** I removed "Any chat can switch from its message box." from the Preferences design board (canvas version 116). The Model row on the board now has no hint. The app still shows "A chat keeps the model it started with." under that row. If you want the app to drop its hint too, tell me.

**Account details and the sign-out line:** there was no reason I couldn't build them, so I did. I've sent you screenshots of Account signed in, in light and dark, and signed out.
- **The new row.** A signed-in account now shows "Email and account details" at the bottom of Account, with an "Open in browser" button. Under it is the line "Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this computer."
- **Where the button goes.** It opens the server's Profile page (`/user_preferences/profile/`). That page shows your email and links to "Manage email addresses". "Delete Account" is in the same page's sidebar. I checked that the page exists on staging: it sends you to the sign-in page first. The production server didn't answer my request, so I couldn't check it there.
- **The local-work note.** "Local work never needs an account…" now shows only when signed out, as the board draws it.

Two things to know:
- **The Profile page is Obico's account settings, not a JusPrin page.** Its sidebar will probably also show Obico items such as "AI Detection Hours" and printer notifications. I haven't seen it while signed in to a JusPrin account.
- **The newer credits drawings of Account leave these rows out.** Those three boards, from 11-02, don't draw the details row or the sign-out line. I found nothing saying that was deliberate, so I went with the main Preferences board.

**Testing:** all 675 page tests pass, including new ones for the row and its button, and the app builds. In the built app the Account page rendered, but I couldn't scroll the window from outside to click the new button. So I checked the button on the same page outside the app, where it sends the right message. I haven't seen the app open the browser.

**The open decision, in plain English:** someday Account will show things like your plan's price with a "Manage plan" button, and a note when a subscription would save you money. Someone has to decide who draws that part of the page.
- **The app draws it**, the way I built the usage chart. Changing a price or a sentence then means shipping a new version of the app, and people on old versions keep seeing the old text.
- **The server draws it**, as a web page shown inside the app. You can change prices without a release, but it's about a day of extra work to sign that page in.

You raised this worry yourself on 11-02, and it was never settled. Nothing is blocked until billing is built, so it can wait until then.

I removed the "Email and account details" row and its "Open in browser" button. It's gone from the Preferences page, from the code behind it in the app, and from the Preferences board on the design canvas (version 117). The line "Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this computer." is still there, and it shows only when you're signed in. The type check passes, all 675 web page tests pass, the app builds, and the 10 agent and brand C++ tests pass.

**Decision needed** (it can wait until billing is built). Once people can buy a plan, Account will show billing details: your plan's price, a "Manage plan" button, and lines like "Bought 500 credits". The question is who draws that part of the screen, the app or our server.

- **The app draws it.** Say you raise the Hobby plan from $5 to $7. Someone running last month's JusPrin still sees $5 until they update. The new price can't reach anyone until we ship a new release.
- **Our server draws it, and the app shows that page in a small built-in browser.** You change the price on the server, and every copy of JusPrin shows $7 the next time Preferences opens, old copies included. This takes about a day of extra work to build. The page may also look slightly different from the rest of the app.

On 11-02 you said prices will change often, a price change shouldn't need an app release, and old copies shouldn't show old prices. That's why I'd pick the server. content.text:
Partly. The server already has a pricing page, but it's the old JusPrin v1 page, so we can't reuse it for this as it stands.

Here's what the server code has today. I read it in tsd-enterprise. I couldn't load jusprinv2.obico.io from this machine because the address didn't resolve.

- **The pricing page at `/ent/jusprin/pricing/`** offers two plans:
  - Free, with 50 credits a month.
  - JusPrin Unlimited, at $6.99 a month or $59.99 a year.

  It checks out through Chargebee, and the checkout code only knows the two Unlimited plans. Its "Back to Chat" link goes to the v1 web chat.
- **The new plans:** Hobby ($10 a month, 750 credits), Workshop ($20 a month, 1,000 credits plus unlimited basic chats) and the 500-credit pack ($10). These exist only as entries in the server's settings file, which is what the credit balance is counted against. They have no page, no checkout and no Chargebee plan in the code.
- **So today**, someone who clicks "Get more credits" in the app ends up on the v1 page, which offers Unlimited.

So the server half you described is what we're building, not something we already have. You've now agreed the billing part of Account is drawn by the server. The credit balance and usage chart I built today stay drawn by the app.

And yes, it needs designing first. I'd propose two design boards on the canvas:

1. **A new pricing page** that offers Hobby, Workshop and the credit pack. It opens from "Get more credits".
2. **The billing part of Preferences › Account**, as the server would draw it inside the app. It holds your plan and its price, a "Manage plan" button, and a list of what you've bought, like "Bought 500 credits". The savings alert and its switch would go here too.

Building them comes after you approve the boards. That means the server pages, the Chargebee plans and checkout, and the small built-in browser in Preferences.

Separately, the credits and usage work from earlier is still uncommitted on jusprin-newui. Tell me if you want it committed now.

0 · Five rules wherever a person meets credits
The boards themselves sit with their flows: On boarding experience, Compositions (beside the Composer), Agent setup & Preferences and Print history. Search “credits” to find them all.
1. One word, one unit, credits only.
It is “credits”, never coins or tokens. A balance is a number of credits and nothing else. Prices in messages appear only on the picker options, the stop card, the pricing page sentence and one scale line under the first-month offer. Dollars appear only where money changes hands.
2. Credits move only when the person sends a message.
Turns the app starts are free, so the balance never changes without a message from the person. On Workshop, Standard messages cost 0 credits.
3. Credits are named by kind, with a date.
Every credit pays for either tier, so bars are grouped only by when credits expire: First-month credits, Free credits and Bought credits, one bar each, and a plan’s monthly credits the same way. After the first month, accounts without a plan get 50 free credits a month, pack holders too; the first month has only the 500. An expiring lot expires one month from the day it was granted; a plan’s credits expire with its billing cycle. The breakdown says once that expiring credits are used first.
4. Say the number before the boundary, not at it.
When the balance runs low the composer says so once, “About 25 credits left”, so reaching it is never news.
5. Nothing typed is lost.
A message that can’t be sent stays in the composer, and nothing stops silently.

def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    return {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }


def _plan(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    subscription = Subscription.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    return {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': bool(subscription and subscription.active()),
        'auto_reload': False,
    }


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def _usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    # The gateway never sees a chat's title, so a row names the chat by its id.
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'tier': row['tier'],
                 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity += report_activity(user, now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or lot.expires_at is not None]
    return {
        'credits': {'total': sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots), 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': _plan(user),
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': _usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
    }

content.text:
Most of it is already designed: the pricing page, the billing part of Account and the savings alert. I also have to correct something I told you last time, and the correction changes the answer.

**What the canvas designs**

- **Pricing page (5a, and 5b for Obico Premium subscribers).** It opens in the browser and has three cards:
  - Pay as you go: $10 once for 500 credits, which never expire. A launch note offers double credits until 31 Jan.
  - Hobby: $10 a month for 750 credits.
  - Workshop: $20 a month for 1,000 credits, and Standard messages cost 0.

  An Obico Premium subscriber sees $8 and $16, with one line saying why. Checkout is Chargebee's hosted page.
- **Preferences › Account (4a to 4c).** This is drawn as one section of the app. It has:
  - A plan line like "Workshop · $16 a month", with the renewal date, the discount line, and "Manage plan" and "Get more credits" buttons.
  - The credit bars and the usage chart.
  - An activity list that includes rows like "Bought 500 credits +500" and "Print report +25".
  - An Alerts checkbox for the savings alert.
- **Savings alert (7a, 7b).** One line above the message box, such as "Hobby would have saved you $5.00 in the last 30 days". It has "See the sums" and "Subscribe".
- **After buying (board 9).** A one-time "+500 credits" line appears when the window gets focus back.

**What's built**

- **In the app:** plan name, renewal date, Get more credits, the bars, the usage chart and the activity list. The list already shows purchase and reward rows once the server sends them.
- **Missing in the app:** the price and discount on the plan line, Manage plan, the Alerts checkbox, the savings alert and the "+500 credits" line.
- **On the server:** none of it. The pricing page is still the v1 page, and checkout only knows the v1 Unlimited plans.

**The correction**

Last time I said that if the app draws the price, changing it needs a new app release. That's wrong. The server's account answer already sends every price (each plan's monthly price, the pack and the price of one credit) and whether the person gets the Obico discount. So if the app draws "$16 a month" from that answer, changing the price on the server changes it in every copy of the app, old copies included. Your reason for wanting server pages is met either way.

A server-drawn page only helps when we add a new kind of offer. For example, a third plan or a new type of card would need a release if the app draws Account.

So my pick is to keep the design as drawn:

- The app draws Account from the server's numbers.
- The pricing page and Chargebee's checkout and "Manage plan" pages open in the browser, the way "Get more credits" already does.
- There's no built-in browser inside Preferences, and Account doesn't need a new design.

Your message ended at "and", so if you meant to ask something more, send the rest.

cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin && git add -u -- resources src tests && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Preferences › Account: show the account's credits and usage

"See usage" on the composer's credits panel opened Preferences › Account,
which showed only the sign-in row. Account now shows, once signed in:

- the plan name (or "Pay as you go") with its renewal date, and a
  "Get more credits" button that opens the server's pricing page in the
  browser, as the composer's button does;
- the credit total and one bar per kind of credit, with what is left and
  when it expires;
- usage for the last 30 days: the total, a bar per day, and a table of
  messages and credits per chat per day, plus print-report rewards, with
  "See all activity" past five rows;
- "Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this
  computer." Signed out, the existing note about working without an
  account stays.

The gateway never sees a chat's title, only a hash of the chat key sent as
X-JusPrin-Chat. So the host keeps a shared file, <data_dir>/jusprin/
chat-titles.json, mapping that hash to the title for every chat that has
a message, and sends the titles the usage table needs with the account.
The hash is now one function, gateway_chat_id(), used by both the request
header and the titles file.

Preferences asks for the account again whenever its window gets focus,
so credits bought in the browser show on return. New design token
component.credits.usageChartHeight (88) sizes the chart.

Tests: Vitest for the section, the focus refresh and the sign-out note;
bridge tests for the titles file; the brand token table.
EOF
